theory.heading: What Experiment Tracking is
theory.body: Experiment Tracking describes the methods and patterns used within AI Engineering to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Experiment Tracking is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Experiment Tracking matters
theory.body: Without Experiment Tracking, systems built with AI Engineering are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Experiment Tracking works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Experiment Tracking follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Experiment Tracking.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Experiment Tracking
theory.body: Experiment Tracking offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
